strings.name: Carl Icahn
strings.role: Investor and chairman of Icahn Enterprises’ general partner
strings.summary: Carl Icahn is an American investor known for using shareholdings to press for changes in corporate governance, capital allocation and restructuring. He founded Icahn & Co. in 1968 and later invested across industries through Icahn Enterprises and affiliates. His activism has prompted debate about short-term returns and long-term corporate development. He also supports education and medical research.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. The general partner’s chairmanship, company CEO, planned succession and completed appointments are distinguished, as are company results and personal wealth. The 2024 SEC settlement retains each party’s penalty and the neither-admit-nor-deny condition.
strings.influence.rationale: Long involved in shareholder activism and corporate acquisitions, influencing governance and restructuring at US public companies.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Graduated in philosophy from Princeton in 1957, then attended NYU medical school; attendance is not recorded as a medical degree.
strings.facts.f2.label: Governance role
strings.facts.f2.value: Chairman of Icahn Enterprises’ general partner since 1990. Someone else serves as company CEO in 2026; Brett Icahn’s succession remains planned.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Pressing for change through ownership
strings.highlights.h1.text: Uses substantial stakes and engagement with management to seek governance and capital-allocation changes; the returns and long-term effects are debated.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Education and medical philanthropy
strings.highlights.h2.text: The family foundation supported Princeton’s genomics laboratory; Mount Sinai’s medical school was renamed for him in recognition of sustained giving.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Icahn Enterprises reports third-quarter results
strings.timeline.t1.text: The company reports a quarterly net loss attributable to IEP of $225 million; this is a company result, not a measure of changes in Icahn’s personal wealth.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Company appoints new CEO
strings.timeline.t2.text: Ted Papapostolou becomes president and CEO; this appointment does not mean Icahn left the general partner’s chairmanship.
strings.timeline.t3.title: SEC settlement over securities-pledge disclosures
strings.timeline.t3.text: Icahn and IEP agree to civil penalties of $500,000 and $1.5 million respectively, without admitting or denying the findings.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Mount Sinai announces medical-school renaming
strings.timeline.t4.text: The institution announces the Icahn name and nearly $200 million in lifetime giving, not a single new $200 million gift.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Foundation supports genomics laboratory
strings.timeline.t5.text: Princeton announces a $20 million gift from the Icahn Family Foundation for laboratory construction.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Becomes general partner’s chairman
strings.timeline.t6.text: The company’s annual report dates his chairmanship of Icahn Enterprises GP to 1990.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Founds Icahn & Co.
strings.timeline.t7.text: Establishes a securities firm focused on arbitrage and options trading, developing an independent investment business.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completes philosophy studies at Princeton
strings.timeline.t8.text: After graduating, he attends medical school before entering finance.
